Yet several of Trump’s actions throw this normally perfunctory question into at least some doubt. articles.summary: The high-profile murder trial of Lindsay Clancy — which ended in a mistrial last week after a jury was unable to convict or acquit the Massachusetts mother in the 2023 strangling deaths of her three young children — put a renewed spotlight on postpartum psychosis, the severe psychiatric condition her lawyers say she was suffering from at the time. As attention moves on from the trial, some researchers want more concrete changes that could improve how postpartum psychosis is researched, treated and prevented. How that happens — and how quickly — is unclear. While some in the mental health community applaud the improvements in how postpartum psychosis is recognized, others think the condition needs a more formal diagnosis for better long-term research. But the overall medical consensus, researchers say, is that postpartum psychosis is treatable when diagnosed early, and that outcomes as severe as Clancy’s are incredibly rare. They hope the trial, which has spurred frank conversations online among mothers about the complexities of postpartum mood and anxiety disorders, can also lead to productive conversations between patients and doctors — instead of panic .
